context:
Goal: mailaudit's Mac test jobs run without blocking or being blocked by the other repos' Mac jobs.
Problem (goal): the Mac-sharing agreement (07:47 CST 11-09) has mailaudit tell four named sessions when its Mac jobs queue and start, and all four are now archived.
Based on (read): list_sessions on 2026-11-15 shows the home, degen and claude-settings sessions from the agreement archived.
Departs from: main, where mailaudit tells four named sessions — changes to telling whichever coordinators run now, or nobody.
Meanwhile: the mailaudit coordinator runs one Mac job at a time and tells nobody.

lastAnswer.note: Owner in chat, 13:09 CST: run Mac jobs as needed and pay no mind to other coordinators.

options.gain: No messages to keep up; mailaudit work keeps moving.
options.how: Mailaudit queues its own Mac jobs, one at a time, and sends no notices.
options.label: Tell nobody; one mailaudit Mac job at a time
options.lose: Another repo's Mac job may wait behind mailaudit without warning.

options.gain: The repos keep sharing the Mac fairly.
options.how: You name the running coordinators; mailaudit tells them when its Mac jobs queue and start.
options.label: Tell the coordinators you name
options.lose: You name the sessions, and each notice costs a little usage.

ref: Mac-sharing agreement among coordinators (07:47 CST 2026-11-09); step cloud-lane-cut (cloud lanes)
reply: Filed as a process-only ruling in docs/debts/notes.md (PR 333): mailaudit runs its Mac jobs as needed and pays no mind to other coordinators. The 2026-11-09 Mac-sharing agreement is retired. Main had no record of it, so a notes line is the home.

shown.label: Tell nobody; one mailaudit Mac job at a time

title: The Mac-sharing agreement names home, degen and claude-settings sessions that are now archived. Who shares the Mac now?
why: Only mailaudit appears to be running now, so the notices have no reader.
